jobs.title: Sill — river-country tileset
jobs.prompt:
Use case: stylized-concept.
Project: Caves of Ooo. Create a polished exploratory pixel-art game asset image grounded in this ORIGINAL game's current Felling lore.
Art direction: "Muted Overgrowth", as refined by its visual identity bible. Crisp deliberately placed pixel clusters, restrained detail, orthographic 3/4 top-down square-grid roguelike view with upright front-facing props; terrain language inspired by 16x16 logical cells, small actors by 16x24 sprites. Consistent apparent pixel size. Flat discrete color steps and sparse speckle, no blurry painterly shading, no smooth gradients, no voxel/isometric diamonds. Terrain has no outlines; discrete props and actors may have a thin dark ink silhouette. Ground lives in middle-dark values; interactables and people have stronger value contrast. Moss ground #2C3226, leaf #46603A / #5D7C44, stone #545C4C / #848C76, bark #5C4A34, bone #AA9E7E / #C4B896. Restrained teal living light and small fungal-magenta accents, warm amber only where appropriate. Mostly muted earth and stone with saturated color spent sparingly on life or magic.
Lore guardrails: present world roughly 1080 years AFTER the Felling of a god-tree. The central tepui is its petrified sandstone stump, fossil anatomy at landscape scale, NOT a fresh wooden stump. The surviving Root sleeps below. Six mortals ascended through six Strikes; a seventh refused. Urqu manifests as loss of identity and absence, NOT a horned monster, eye, purple corruption, or deliberate evil. Preserve mystery; show places, not an authoritative illustration of disputed history. The setting balances ordinary domestic life, strange ecology, and cosmic unease.
This is a potential art-direction study, not a claim of an engine-ready sliced atlas. No franchise logos, UI, watermark, text paragraphs, or invented lore.
Asset type: landscape pixel-art TILESET CONCEPT SHEET, one image, 3:2 aspect. A quiet dark moss studio backing, uniform spacious gutters, precisely aligned modular tile swatches and isolated sprite props. All tiles at the same scale and same camera. Short plain bone-white pixel lettering only at top: "SILL / THE SPREAD"; small row captions "GROUND", "RIVER", "BUILDINGS", "LIFE". Main focus is the actual modular art, no decorative framing.
Layout: four orderly horizontal shelves of distinct usable concepts. GROUND: grass variants, worked earth, packed lane, grass/lane edge and corner transitions, hedgerow segments with a stile. RIVER: muted dark-teal water variants, muddy bank straight/inner/outer corners, reeds, stepping-stone ford, river-stone bank. BUILDINGS: timber and river-stone thatched house modules, roof and wall segment variations, door with worn tiny tree carving on lintel, mill waterwheel, small plank landing, drying rack, portable merchant stall with balance scales and berry/honey goods. LIFE: small moss-cloaked traveler and ordinary villagers, geese, reedfrog, clay vessel, fishing basket, simple river-shrine with bread and salt, a modest patch of conjured pink flowers.
Sill is a practical farming and fishing village on a slow river. Most objects are mundane and repaired; cosmology is a children's story here. The shrine is for a local river power, not a giant Tree temple. Do not add oversized fantasy mushrooms or glowing machinery. Distinct silhouettes and broad simple clusters must read as plausible tiny sprites. Equal spacing and no overlaps.

Warm ordinary life, believable repaired materials, gentle melancholy. Surface light is mundane sunlight, not giant glowing fungi. Nothing overtly apocalyptic. No vast god-tree or floating icons, no HUD. Plenty of readable negative space between interactables.

Mood is immense age, stillness, and an unfinished act felt in a physical place. No flashback, gods striking, or attempt to explain the seventh refusal.

Scene: a lived-in catacomb village beneath the petrified tree country. Orthographic 3/4 top-down cutaway game view: a roughly oval excavated main chamber organized around a low cultivated glowing fungal hearth-patch. The patch is ringed by wine-red Drosera sundews with one clear tending gap; compact spores glow magenta and pale lilac. Clearly walkable stone floor circulates around it. Three tiers of rectangular wall niches contain folded mycelial-fiber bedding and ordinary stored belongings, connected by carved steps and a rope ladder. The same niches are homes and future tombs, expressed as a gentle domestic detail. A plaque wall of tiny individual carved records, oldest low down, is visibly tended; one small smoothed-away patch interrupts it.
At the entrance: a Pebble-Sundew mat beneath a dark Choir-Iron lintel, with small green slime-paint wayfinding marks. Secondary light comes from discrete teal Glow-Quartz seams and lantern-beetle jars carried by residents. A side cistern and little beetle hatchery make the chamber practical. Beyond the lantern boundary, one side passage becomes truly black; lighting shapes the safe navigable room.
Small residents in pale, moss and mycelial cloth: one tends the central patch, two share plain bowls in the hearth glow, a child sits beside folded bedding in a niche with a little cave-rat. A tiny traveler arrives at the threshold. No giant god figure: this is an ordinary inhabited village whose light has a sacred source. Quiet kindness and deep strangeness together. No bonfires/torches, no skull dungeon, no excessive glowing mushrooms, no bright uniform cave ambient light, no UI or text. Broad readable pixels and controlled localized color, not painterly realism.
